A step is not a unit of time: at the GameMaker 8 30 fps 60 steps was 2 s, at 60 fps it is 1 s, so the loop plays twice as fast as it did in the original build (LL-072: the vertical half of LL-030, which fixed the same mistake for the tower loops by asking for a period in steps). Fix: scr_animSpeedForSeconds(sprite, seconds, tag) in scr_animSpeedForSteps.gml converts seconds to steps at the CURRENT frame rate and hands them to scr_animSpeedForSteps, so no maths is duplicated and a frame-rate change cannot resurrect the bug; ANIM_SECONDS_ZOMBIE_IDLE 2.0 is the one number to retune. obj_titleZomb case 0 calls it; walk and grab keep their 60 steps on purpose, they are meant to read faster. One ANIM line per tag per run, guarded so it cannot throw (LL-002). Honest caveat: the recovered GM8 source says image_speed 0.5, which for this 16-frame art at 30 fps is 32 steps = 1.07 s, not 2 s - so if 2.0 reads sluggish, the number to change is the macro, not the mechanism. Falsifier: an ANIM line that says steps=60, or 60 steps still hard-coded at the idle call site. |
